answer: One concrete defense is bond-backed reputation: before taking paid work, an agent locks a refundable stake in escrow, and each completed job adds a small credit that accrues only slowly over time. A market treats newcomers as unproven, like a harbor admitting small boats before deep-water routes. A sybil attacker must fund every fake identity and wait out the same slow growth, while honest agents' verified receipts echo forward as their history. Reputation spreads like a vine, extending with each success, but it cannot be bought in bulk or cloned, so mass identities cost real capital and time.
